entry.name: pattr
entry.digest: Provide an alias with a named data wrapper
entry.description: Stores its own data, or binds to another object to share its contents with other pattr-based objects (such as pattrstorage). Can be used for data routing or preset creation.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: A symbol argument may be optionally used to set theobject's. In the absence of an argument (or the explicit setting of theattribute using thesyntax), theobject is given an arbitrary, semi-random name, such as u197000004.

attributes.name: annotation_name
attributes.digest: Info View Title

attributes.name: autorestore
attributes.digest: Automatic restore state
attributes.description: Enables (1) or disables (0) the autorestore state of theobject. The default is 1 (enabled). When enabled, theobject will automatically output its last-saved value when the patcher is loaded (and, if bound to another object, send the value to that object. See theattribute, below for more information on bound objects).

attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: bindto
attributes.digest: Named object binding
attributes.description: The word, which may be followed by an optionalargument, sets theobject's binding state. The default state is unbound (no arguments). By default, theobject maintains its own data. When "bound" using thefeature, aobject maintains the data for the other object and automatically gets and sets values for that object.takes an optionalargument, which specifies the name of the object to whichwill bind. Binding targets need not be at the same patcher-level as theobject. In this case, a double-colon syntax ('::') is used to separate levels of patcher hierarchy for the purposes of describing a path for name resolution (e.g. somepatcher::someobject). If the named object is at a higher patcher-level than the pattr object, the word parent can be used to refer to a patcher at a higher level (e.g. parent::objectaboveme, parent::parent::objectaboveobjectaboveme or).If the named object contains attributes, and the user wishes to bind to a specific attribute, the same double-colon syntax is used to specify the name of that attribute (e.g. someobject::someattribute). Amessage sent without an argument unbinds theobject from any bound object, and causes it to resume the maintenance its own internal state. See the pattr helpfile for more information about this feature.

attributes.name: thru
attributes.digest: Throughput mode
attributes.description: Adjusts theobject's thru behavior. The default is 1 (Output value on change). When enabled for all change, the object will output its value whenever it changes, or in response to a bang. When set to 0 (Suppress output on change (bang only)), the object will only output its value when it receives amessage. When set to 2 (Suppress output when triggered from inlet), the value will be output upon change which wasn't triggered by a message to theobject's inlet.

choices.value: Suppress output when triggered from inlet
